FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE March 9, 2026 COEUR D’ALENE — C hrista Hazel has announced she will seek the Idaho House of Representatives seat for Legislative D istrict 4B in the May 2026 Republican primary. “I love Idaho. I love C oeur d’A lene. This is home, and our community deserves strong representation in B oise,” Hazel said. Hazel grew up in the Hayden C reek area and later settled in C oeur d’A lene, where she and her husband raised their family. She graduated from C oeur d’A lene High School and North Idaho C ollege before earning her bachelor’s and law degrees from the University of Idaho, where she served on the Law Review. Hazel has been active in community leadership for more than a decade. She was elected to the C oeur d’A lene School B oard in 2013 and served until 2017, including two years as board chair. Prior to her election, she co-chaired the successful 2012 school bond effort that funded improvements for local schools. In 2016, Hazel was also elected to serve as a precinct committeewoman on the Kootenai C ounty Republican C entral C ommittee. “Idahoans know how to solve Idaho’s problems,” Hazel said. “We don’t need outside political groups telling our communities what to do.” Hazel said her decision to run comes from years of civic involvement and a belief that government works best when leaders stay focused on the communities they serve. “When elected leaders stay focused on the people they serve and the issues that affect our communities, families and businesses can thrive,” Hazel said. “When leaders lose focus, taxpayers often pay the price — something our community experienced during the turmoil at North Idaho C ollege.” Hazel said her approach to public service is grounded in the principles she tries to live by. “I’m a Republican not simply because of party affiliation, but because those principles guide how I live my life,” Hazel said. “Faith, family and freedom aren’t slogans to me — they are responsibilities.” “Families work hard for their money. They’re accountable for how they spend it and must live within a budget,” Hazel said. “Government should do the same.” “I don’t like wasteful spending and I don’t like government overreach,” Hazel said. “Idaho families expect their leaders to be responsible with taxpayer dollars and focused on the needs of our communities.”

# Page 2^page=2
Hazel said her priorities in the Legislature include protecting local control, keeping taxes low, supporting strong schools and workforce opportunities, and ensuring government remains accountable to the people it serves. A cancer survivor, Hazel believes access to quality health care close to home is critical for Idaho families. Hazel and her husband, Joel Hazel, have been married for 26 years. Joel Hazel is a former prosecutor and now serves as a healthcare executive in the region. Their son is enrolled in a graduate program at B oise State University, and their daughter is pursuing a healthcare-related degree at North Idaho C ollege. Hazel said she understands the race will attract attention but plans to keep her campaign focused on issues important to North Idaho families. She will spend the coming weeks meeting with voters across Legislative D istrict 4B . The Republican primary election will be held May 19, 2026. ### CONTACT: C hrista Hazel for C dA 208/771-0073
